foods.name: Ewedu (jute leaves)
foods.forms: Cooked and drawn into a smooth soup

foods.name: Scent leaf
foods.forms: Fresh herb added at end of cooking

foods.name: Palm fruit
foods.forms: Boiled and extracted for soup base

foods.name: Assorted meat (beef, tripe, cow skin etc.)
Yaji (suya spice)
foods.forms: Ground blend of kuli-kuli, ginger, garlic, paprika, cayenne

foods.name: Stock / seasoning cubes
foods.allergenNote: Check label (may contain gluten, soy, milk, celery)

recipes.name: Jollof Rice
recipes.summaryIngredients: Long-grain parboiled rice, tomatoes, tatashe, scotch bonnet, onions, stock
recipes.healthBenefits: Tomatoes and peppers supply antioxidants (lycopene, vitamin C); rice gives quick energy; onions support heart health.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, vitamin C, vitamin A, lycopene
recipes.cautions: High in carbs and oil. Use less oil, add veggies (carrots, peas) and pair with protein and salad.
recipes.servedWith: Fried plantain, chicken/beef, coleslaw, moi moi
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool quickly, refrigerate within 1 hr; eat within 1 day; reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Low heat + tight foil cover = evenly cooked grains. Don't stir too often or it turns mushy.

ingredientLines.rawText: 2 stock cubes, 1 tsp curry, 1 tsp thyme, 2 bay leaves

steps.instruction: Blend tomatoes, tatashe, scotch bonnet and 1 onion until smooth; boil the blend down until thick (about 15 min).
Heat oil, fry sliced onion until soft, add tomato paste and fry 5 min.
Add the reduced pepper blend and fry 15-20 min until oil floats on top.
Add stock, seasoning cubes, curry, thyme, bay leaves and salt; bring to a boil.
Wash rice, add to the pot, stir, cover with foil and lid; cook on low heat 30-35 min.
Stir gently, check doneness, add butter and let it slightly catch at the bottom for the smoky 'party' flavour.

recipes.name: Fried Rice (Nigerian)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Parboiled rice, mixed vegetables, liver, curry, stock
recipes.healthBenefits: Vegetables add fibre and vitamins; liver is rich in iron and vitamin B12, good for blood health.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, fibre, iron, vitamin A, B12
recipes.cautions: Can be oily. Stir-fry with minimal oil and load up on vegetables.
recipes.servedWith: Fried chicken, plantain, salad
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool quickly, refrigerate within 1 hr; eat within 1 day; reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Use cooled, dry rice so it fries rather than steams. Curry gives the signature yellow colour.

ingredientLines.rawText: 2 tsp curry, 1 tsp thyme, 2 stock cubes

steps.instruction: Cook rice in stock with curry, thyme and salt until just done and dry; spread out to cool.
Boil liver in seasoned water 10 min, then dice.
Heat a little oil, stir-fry onions, then add vegetables and liver for 3-4 min (keep them crunchy).
Add cooled rice in batches, stirring so every grain is coated.
Adjust seasoning and serve.

recipes.name: Egusi Soup
recipes.summaryIngredients: Ground melon seeds, palm oil, leafy vegetables, assorted meat, stockfish
recipes.healthBenefits: Egusi seeds are rich in protein and healthy fats; leafy greens give iron and folate; supports muscle building and satiety.
recipes.keyNutrients: Protein, healthy fats, vitamin E, iron, folate
recipes.cautions: Calorie-dense due to seeds and palm oil. Moderate portions; use less palm oil.
recipes.servedWith: Pounded yam, eba, fufu, semo, amala
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Frying egusi before adding stock gives a richer taste and prevents a raw 'seedy' flavour.

ingredientLines.rawText: 1 kg assorted meat (beef, shaki, cow skin)
2 cups chopped ugu or spinach (or bitterleaf)

steps.instruction: Season and boil meat with onion and stock cubes until tender; add stockfish and dry fish.
Mix egusi with a little water/onion into a paste.
Heat palm oil, add egusi paste in lumps (or stir for smooth style) and fry 10 min, stirring to avoid burning.
Add meat stock gradually, then meat, fish, crayfish and pepper; simmer 15 min.
Add vegetables, cook 3-5 min, adjust salt and serve.

recipes.name: Efo Riro
recipes.summaryIngredients: Spinach/efo tete, tatashe, palm oil, locust beans, assorted meat
recipes.healthBenefits: Very high in leafy greens - iron, calcium, vitamin K and antioxidants; iru (locust beans) aids digestion.
recipes.keyNutrients: Iron, calcium, vitamins A, C, K, protein
recipes.cautions: Don't overcook the vegetables or you lose nutrients. Use palm oil moderately.
recipes.servedWith: Pounded yam, eba, amala, white rice
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Squeezing water from the greens keeps the stew thick and rich, not watery.

ingredientLines.rawText: 2 large bunches efo tete or spinach

steps.instruction: Wash, chop and blanch vegetables briefly; squeeze out water.
Boil meat with seasoning until tender.
Heat palm oil, fry onions and iru, add pepper blend and fry until reduced (15 min).
Add meat, fish, crayfish and seasoning; simmer 5 min.
Stir in vegetables, cook 2-3 min and serve.

recipes.name: Ogbono Soup
recipes.summaryIngredients: Ground ogbono (wild mango seed), palm oil, okra or greens, meat/fish
recipes.healthBenefits: Ogbono is high in fibre and may help regulate blood sugar and cholesterol; supports digestion.
recipes.keyNutrients: Fibre, healthy fats, protein, iron
recipes.cautions: Palm-oil heavy versions are calorie-rich. Combine with okra for extra fibre.
recipes.servedWith: Eba, fufu, pounded yam
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Don't fry ogbono on high heat - it loses its draw. Less stirring = more draw.

steps.instruction: Boil meat and stockfish with seasoning until tender.
Heat palm oil on low heat, take off heat and stir in ogbono until it dissolves.
Return to heat, add meat stock gradually while stirring until it draws.
Add meat, fish, crayfish, pepper; simmer 10-15 min stirring often.
Add greens, cook 3 min and serve.

recipes.name: Afang Soup
recipes.summaryIngredients: Afang (okazi) leaves, waterleaf, periwinkle, palm oil, meat/fish
recipes.healthBenefits: Very nutrient-dense; afang and waterleaf are rich in fibre, iron and antioxidants; periwinkle adds zinc and protein.
recipes.keyNutrients: Fibre, iron, zinc, protein, vitamins A & C
recipes.cautions: Use moderate palm oil. Wash periwinkle thoroughly.
recipes.servedWith: Pounded yam, eba, fufu
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Don't add water - the waterleaf releases enough liquid.

ingredientLines.rawText: 2 cups afang leaves (pounded or finely ground)
1 kg assorted meat, kpomo, stockfish, dry fish

steps.instruction: Boil meats with seasoning until tender; add stockfish and dry fish.
Add waterleaf first and cook 5 min (it releases water).
Add palm oil, crayfish, pepper and periwinkle; cook 5 min.
Add the ground afang leaves, stir well, cook 5 min.
Adjust seasoning and serve.

recipes.name: Edikang Ikong
recipes.summaryIngredients: Ugu (pumpkin leaves), waterleaf, periwinkle, palm oil, meat
recipes.healthBenefits: Often called a 'vegetable powerhouse'; ugu is linked to improved blood health (iron) and immunity.
recipes.keyNutrients: Iron, folate, vitamins A, C, K, protein
recipes.cautions: Very high in greens - one of the healthiest Nigerian soups. Keep oil moderate.
recipes.servedWith: Pounded yam, fufu, eba
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Ratio is usually more ugu than waterleaf so the soup isn't watery.

steps.instruction: Cook meats with very little water and seasoning until tender.
Add waterleaf, cook 5 min.
Add palm oil, crayfish, pepper and periwinkle; stir.
Add ugu, stir, cook 3-5 min and serve.

recipes.name: Banga Soup (Ofe Akwu)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Palm fruit extract, banga spices, catfish, beletete leaves
recipes.healthBenefits: Palm fruit is rich in vitamin E (tocotrienols) and beta-carotene - antioxidants that support skin and eyes.
recipes.keyNutrients: Vitamin E, vitamin A, healthy fats, protein (fish)
recipes.cautions: Naturally high in fat. Skim excess oil and keep portions moderate.
recipes.servedWith: Starch (Delta), white rice (Igbo ofe akwu), eba
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Don't stir after adding catfish so it doesn't break apart.

ingredientLines.rawText: 1 kg palm fruits (or 800g tinned palm concentrate)
2 tbsp crayfish, pepper, stock cubes, salt

steps.instruction: Boil palm fruits until soft, pound and extract the juice with warm water; sieve.
Boil the extract 20 min until it thickens and oil rises.
Add cooked meat, crayfish, pepper and banga spices.
Add cleaned catfish gently, simmer 10 min.
Add beletete/scent leaves, simmer 3 min, serve.

recipes.name: Okra Soup
recipes.summaryIngredients: Fresh okra, palm oil, ugu, meat/fish, crayfish
recipes.healthBenefits: Okra is rich in soluble fibre - supports digestion, may help control blood sugar and cholesterol; low in calories.
recipes.keyNutrients: Fibre, vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, magnesium
recipes.cautions: Great option for weight watchers and diabetics (with a portion-controlled swallow).
recipes.servedWith: Eba, fufu, semo, amala
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: A pinch of potash (akanwu) increases the draw, but use sparingly.

steps.instruction: Boil meat with seasoning until tender.
Add palm oil, crayfish, pepper and fish; simmer 5 min.
Add okra, stir, cook 3-5 min (don't overcook - keep it green).
Add ugu, cook 2 min, serve.

recipes.name: Goat Meat Pepper Soup
recipes.summaryIngredients: Goat meat, pepper soup spice, scent leaves, scotch bonnet
recipes.healthBenefits: Light broth that's warming; spices (uda, uziza, ehuru) have anti-inflammatory properties; traditionally given for colds and postpartum recovery.
recipes.keyNutrients: Protein, iron, zinc, B vitamins
recipes.cautions: Low-carb and low-oil. Watch sodium from stock cubes.
recipes.servedWith: Boiled yam, white rice, agidi, on its own
recipes.occasion: Evenings, bars, cold weather, new mothers
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Catfish (point-and-kill) or chicken work with the same method - just shorter cooking.

ingredientLines.rawText: Handful of scent leaves (efirin) or uziza

steps.instruction: Wash goat meat, season with onion, stock cubes and salt; steam 10 min.
Add water and boil until meat is almost tender (40 min).
Add pepper soup spice and ground pepper; simmer 10 min.
Add sliced scent leaves, cook 2 min, serve hot.

recipes.name: Ofe Onugbu (Bitterleaf Soup)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Washed bitterleaf, cocoyam thickener, palm oil, ogiri, meat/fish
recipes.healthBenefits: Bitterleaf has been studied for blood-sugar-lowering and antimicrobial effects; supports liver health and digestion.
recipes.keyNutrients: Fibre, antioxidants, vitamin C, iron
recipes.cautions: Ensure leaves are properly washed to reduce bitterness. Cocoyam thickener adds carbs.
recipes.servedWith: Fufu, pounded yam, eba
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Ogiri gives the authentic aroma; substitute with iru if unavailable.

steps.instruction: Boil meat and stockfish with seasoning until tender.
Add palm oil, pepper, crayfish and ogiri; cook 5 min.
Add pounded cocoyam in small lumps; cook until dissolved and soup thickens (10 min).
Add bitterleaf, simmer 5 min, adjust salt and serve.

recipes.name: Moi Moi
recipes.summaryIngredients: Peeled beans, tatashe, onions, oil, eggs/fish
recipes.healthBenefits: Steamed, not fried - beans give plant protein and fibre; good for heart health and steady blood sugar.
recipes.keyNutrients: Plant protein, fibre, folate, iron, potassium
recipes.cautions: Use less oil (2-3 tbsp is enough per 2 cups beans). Great for diabetics in moderation.
recipes.servedWith: Jollof, pap (ogi), custard, garri, bread
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh; cool fully, store covered and eat within 2-3 days.
recipes.tips: Whisking the batter for a few minutes makes it lighter and fluffier.

steps.instruction: Soak beans 10 min, rub to remove skins, rinse until clean.
Blend beans with peppers and onion to a smooth thick paste.
Mix in oil, stock, stock cubes and salt to a pourable (not watery) consistency.
Pour into leaves, foil or ramekins; add egg/fish.
Steam 45-60 min until firm.

recipes.name: Akara (Bean Cakes)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Peeled beans, onions, pepper, oil for frying
recipes.healthBenefits: High in plant protein from beans - filling and energy-giving breakfast.
recipes.keyNutrients: Plant protein, fibre, iron
recipes.cautions: Deep fried - absorbs oil. Drain on paper towels; air-frying is a healthier option.
recipes.servedWith: Pap (ogi/akamu), bread, custard
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh; cool fully, store covered and eat within 2-3 days.
recipes.tips: Too much water = flat akara that soaks up oil. Keep the batter thick.

steps.instruction: Soak and peel beans; rinse well.
Blend with very little water to a thick paste.
Whisk paste vigorously 5 min to add air; add chopped onion, pepper and salt.
Scoop spoonfuls into hot oil, fry until golden on both sides.
Drain and serve hot.

recipes.name: Suya
recipes.summaryIngredients: Thin beef slices, yaji (suya spice), groundnut oil
recipes.healthBenefits: Lean beef provides protein, iron and zinc; spices like ginger and garlic aid digestion.
recipes.keyNutrients: Protein, iron, zinc, B12
recipes.cautions: Grilled meat over open flame - avoid charring. Yaji has groundnut (allergy warning).
recipes.servedWith: Sliced onions, tomatoes, cabbage, extra yaji
recipes.storageGuidance: Cook fresh; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hrs, eat within 2 days and reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Soak wooden skewers in water 30 min to stop them burning.

ingredientLines.rawText: 1/2 cup yaji (ground kuli-kuli, ginger, garlic, paprika, cayenne, stock cube)

steps.instruction: Slice beef very thin and thread onto skewers.
Brush with oil, coat generously with yaji.
Marinate 2 hrs or overnight.
Grill on high heat or oven 200°C, 8-10 min per side, brushing with oil.
Sprinkle extra yaji and serve with onions and tomatoes.

recipes.name: Pounded Yam
recipes.summaryIngredients: White yam, water
recipes.healthBenefits: Yam provides complex carbs, potassium and vitamin C; naturally gluten-free.
recipes.keyNutrients: Complex carbs, potassium, vitamin C, fibre
recipes.cautions: High glycemic load in big portions. Keep the swallow fist-sized and eat with veggie-rich soup.
recipes.servedWith: Egusi, efo riro, ogbono, afang, edikang ikong
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hrs and eat within 1-2 days.
recipes.tips: Use old (dry) yam - new yam is watery and gives a soft, sticky result.

steps.instruction: Peel yam, cut into chunks and wash.
Boil until very soft (20-25 min).
Pound in a mortar (or use a food processor/yam pounder) while hot, adding a splash of hot water.
Pound until smooth, stretchy and lump-free; shape into balls.

recipes.name: Eba (Garri)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Garri (fermented cassava granules), hot water
recipes.healthBenefits: Quick energy source; fermentation of cassava may support gut health.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, some fibre
recipes.cautions: Low in protein and vitamins on its own - pair with protein-rich, vegetable soup. Yellow garri has some vitamin A (palm oil).
recipes.servedWith: Okra, ogbono, egusi, efo riro
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hrs and eat within 1-2 days.
recipes.tips: Adding garri to water (not water to garri) prevents lumps.

steps.instruction: Pour boiling water into a bowl.
Sprinkle garri over the water and let it soak 1 min.
Stir and fold firmly with a wooden spatula until smooth.
Add more garri for firmer eba; shape and serve.

recipes.name: Amala, Ewedu & Gbegiri
recipes.summaryIngredients: Yam flour, jute leaves, peeled beans, palm oil, stew
recipes.healthBenefits: Ewedu (jute leaves) is high in iron and fibre; gbegiri adds plant protein; amala (yam flour) has a lower glycemic index than pounded yam.
recipes.keyNutrients: Fibre, iron, plant protein, vitamins A & C
recipes.cautions: Balanced combo - carbs + protein + greens. Watch the oily stew topping.
recipes.servedWith: Assorted meat, buka stew (ata dindin)
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Stir amala fast and continuously to avoid lumps.

ingredientLines.rawText: Buka stew and assorted meat to serve

steps.instruction: Gbegiri: boil peeled beans until very soft, mash smooth; add palm oil, crayfish, pepper, seasoning; simmer 10 min.
Ewedu: pick leaves, boil in a little water (with potash if using) 5 min; whisk (ijabe) until slimy, add iru, crayfish, salt.
Amala: boil water, sprinkle elubo while stirring vigorously; add a splash of water, cover 3 min, stir again until smooth.
Serve amala with ewedu, gbegiri and stew on top.

recipes.name: Beans Porridge (Ewa Riro)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Honey beans, palm oil, onions, pepper, crayfish
recipes.healthBenefits: Excellent plant protein and fibre; keeps you full; supports heart health and steady blood sugar.
recipes.keyNutrients: Plant protein, fibre, folate, magnesium, potassium
recipes.cautions: Can cause bloating - parboil and discard first water to reduce gas.
recipes.servedWith: Fried plantain (dodo), bread, garri
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Pressure cooker cuts cooking time by half.

steps.instruction: Pick and wash beans; boil 10 min, drain water.
Add fresh water, cook until soft (45-60 min).
In a separate pan, fry onion and pepper blend in palm oil 10 min.
Pour into beans with crayfish, seasoning and fish; simmer 10 min, mashing some beans for creaminess.
Serve.

recipes.name: Yam Porridge (Asaro)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Yam, palm oil, pepper blend, greens, fish
recipes.healthBenefits: Comforting, easy to digest; yam offers potassium and vitamin C; greens add iron.
recipes.keyNutrients: Complex carbs, potassium, vitamin C, iron
recipes.cautions: Add vegetables and fish to balance the carbs.
recipes.servedWith: Eaten on its own
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Sweet potato or plantain can be added for a twist.

steps.instruction: Peel and cube yam, wash, put in pot with water just covering it.
Add pepper blend, palm oil, crayfish, fish and seasoning.
Cook until yam is soft (20 min); mash some pieces to thicken.
Add greens, stir and cook 2 min. Serve.

recipes.name: Ofada Rice & Ayamase
recipes.summaryIngredients: Local unpolished ofada rice, green peppers, bleached palm oil, iru, assorted meat
recipes.healthBenefits: Ofada rice is unpolished - more fibre, minerals and lower glycemic index than white rice.
recipes.keyNutrients: Fibre, B vitamins, magnesium, protein
recipes.cautions: Ayamase uses lots of bleached palm oil - reduce quantity. Bleaching oil produces smoke; do it outdoors.
recipes.servedWith: Fried plantain, boiled eggs
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool quickly, refrigerate within 1 hr; eat within 1 day; reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Traditionally served in uma (moimoi) leaves for aroma.

ingredientLines.rawText: 10 green bell peppers + 4 green scotch bonnet

steps.instruction: Pick stones from ofada rice, wash well, boil until soft (40-50 min).
Coarsely blend green peppers and boil to reduce water.
Bleach palm oil: heat in a covered pot on low heat 10-15 min until clear (ventilate!). Cool slightly.
Fry onions and iru in the oil, add pepper blend and fry 20-30 min.
Add cooked meat, stock and seasoning; simmer 10 min; add eggs.

recipes.name: Nkwobi
recipes.summaryIngredients: Cow foot, palm oil, potash (akanwu), utazi, ugba
recipes.healthBenefits: Cow foot is rich in collagen and gelatin, which support joints and skin.
recipes.keyNutrients: Protein, collagen, healthy fats
recipes.cautions: High in fat and cholesterol - an occasional treat. Potash in small amounts only.
recipes.servedWith: Palm wine, chilled drinks
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Serve in a wooden bowl for the classic presentation.

steps.instruction: Boil cow foot with seasoning until very tender (1.5 hrs); reduce stock.
Mix filtered potash water into palm oil until it thickens and turns yellow.
Add crayfish, ehuru, pepper and a little stock; mix into a paste.
Toss cow foot in the paste and warm through.
Garnish with sliced utazi and onions.

recipes.name: Fried Plantain (Dodo)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Ripe plantain, salt, oil
recipes.healthBenefits: Plantain provides potassium, vitamin A, vitamin C and fibre; good for heart health.
recipes.keyNutrients: Potassium, vitamins A, B6, C, fibre
recipes.cautions: Deep-fried absorbs oil. Air-fry or roast (boli) for a healthier version.
recipes.servedWith: Jollof, beans, rice and stew, eggs
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh; store covered and eat within 1-2 days.
recipes.tips: Very ripe plantain caramelises faster - lower the heat slightly.

steps.instruction: Peel plantain and cut diagonally or into cubes.
Sprinkle lightly with salt.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown on both sides (3-4 min).
Drain on paper towel and serve.

recipes.name: Boli (Roasted Plantain)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Ripe plantain, groundnuts, fish/pepper sauce
recipes.healthBenefits: Roasted, not fried - a lower-fat way to enjoy plantain's potassium and fibre; groundnuts add protein and healthy fats.
recipes.keyNutrients: Potassium, fibre, vitamins A & C, healthy fats
recipes.cautions: One of the healthier snacks. Groundnut allergy warning.
recipes.servedWith: Roasted groundnuts, roasted fish & pepper sauce
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh; cool fully, store covered and eat within 2-3 days.
recipes.tips: Slightly firm plantain roasts best; very soft ones turn mushy.

ingredientLines.rawText: Pepper sauce: palm oil, scotch bonnet, onion, salt

steps.instruction: Peel plantains.
Roast over charcoal, grill or oven (200°C) turning until charred spots appear and inside is soft (20-25 min).
Make pepper sauce by mixing palm oil, ground pepper, onions and salt.
Serve with groundnuts and sauce.

recipes.name: Puff-Puff
recipes.summaryIngredients: Flour, sugar, yeast, nutmeg, oil
recipes.healthBenefits: Quick energy treat - mainly an indulgence rather than a health food.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates
recipes.cautions: High in sugar and oil. Enjoy occasionally; reduce sugar to 1/4 cup.
recipes.servedWith: Zobo, chilled drinks, small chops platter
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh; store covered and eat within 1-2 days.
recipes.tips: Oil should be medium-hot - too hot and the inside stays raw.

steps.instruction: Mix flour, sugar, yeast, nutmeg and salt.
Add warm water gradually, mix into a smooth sticky batter.
Cover and leave to rise 45-60 min until doubled.
Scoop small balls with your hand into hot oil; fry until golden.
Drain and serve.

recipes.name: Chin Chin
recipes.summaryIngredients: Flour, sugar, butter, milk, eggs, nutmeg
recipes.healthBenefits: Energy-dense snack; eggs and milk add a little protein and calcium.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, fats, some protein
recipes.cautions: High in sugar and fat. Bake instead of frying for a lighter version.
recipes.servedWith: Drinks, tea
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool fully; store airtight in a cool, dry place; discard if stale, rancid-smelling or mouldy.
recipes.tips: Popular as a small business product - good packaging sells.

steps.instruction: Mix flour, sugar, nutmeg and baking powder; rub in butter until crumbly.
Add egg and milk; knead into a firm dough.
Roll out thin, cut into small squares/strips.
Fry in medium-hot oil, stirring, until golden.
Drain, cool and store in an airtight jar.

recipes.name: Tuwo Shinkafa & Miyan Kuka
recipes.summaryIngredients: Soft rice, baobab leaf powder, dried meat/fish, daddawa
recipes.healthBenefits: Baobab leaves are rich in calcium, iron, and antioxidants; supports bone health and immunity.
recipes.keyNutrients: Calcium, iron, vitamin C, fibre, carbs
recipes.cautions: Balanced meal. Keep oil moderate.
recipes.servedWith: Miyan kuka, miyan taushe, miyan kubewa (okra)
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Whisk continuously while adding kuka or it clumps.

steps.instruction: Tuwo: cook rice with extra water until very soft; mash/stir vigorously into a smooth mass; shape.
Kuka: boil meat/fish with onion, pepper, daddawa and seasoning.
Add oil, then sprinkle kuka powder while whisking to avoid lumps.
Simmer 5 min and serve with tuwo.

recipes.name: Masa (Waina)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Rice, yeast, sugar, oil
recipes.healthBenefits: Fermented rice cakes - fermentation improves digestibility; lighter than deep-fried snacks.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, some B vitamins
recipes.cautions: Pair with protein-rich soup/suya for balance.
recipes.servedWith: Miyan taushe, yaji, honey, suya
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh; cool fully, store covered and eat within 2-3 days.
recipes.tips: A special masa pan with round holes gives the authentic shape.

steps.instruction: Blend soaked rice and cooked rice with a little water to a thick batter.
Add yeast, cover and ferment 2 hrs (or overnight).
Add sugar, salt, baking powder; mix.
Pour into an oiled masa pan (or muffin pan) and cook covered on low heat; flip once golden.

recipes.name: Abacha (African Salad)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Dried shredded cassava, ugba, palm oil, potash, garden egg leaves, fish
recipes.healthBenefits: Ugba (fermented oil bean) contains probiotics and protein; garden egg leaves add fibre and iron.
recipes.keyNutrients: Fibre, protein, probiotics, vitamin A
recipes.cautions: Potash in small amounts only; not ideal for people with kidney issues.
recipes.servedWith: Fried fish, kpomo, garden eggs, palm wine
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Serve at room temperature - it's a salad.

ingredientLines.rawText: Garden egg leaves or utazi, onions
Fried fish, kpomo, stock cubes, salt

steps.instruction: Soak abacha in cold water 10 min until soft; drain.
Mix filtered potash water into palm oil until it thickens.
Add crayfish, pepper, ehuru, stock cube and ugba; mix.
Add abacha and mix thoroughly.
Top with sliced garden egg leaves, onions and fish.

recipes.name: Zobo Drink
recipes.summaryIngredients: Dried hibiscus petals, ginger, pineapple, cloves
recipes.healthBenefits: Hibiscus is rich in antioxidants; studies link it to lowering blood pressure; ginger aids digestion.
recipes.keyNutrients: Antioxidants (anthocyanins), vitamin C
recipes.cautions: Commercial zobo can be very sugary - sweeten with fruit (pineapple, dates) instead.
recipes.servedWith: Small chops, puff-puff, on its own
recipes.storageGuidance: Keep chilled in a clean covered container; drink within 1-2 days; discard if it smells off.
recipes.tips: Popular small-business drink - add cucumber or orange for flavour variants.

steps.instruction: Wash zobo leaves.
Boil with pineapple peels, ginger and cloves 20-30 min.
Cool and strain.
Blend pineapple flesh, strain and add to the drink for natural sweetness.
Refrigerate and serve chilled.

recipes.name: Kunu (Kunun Zaki)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Millet or sorghum, ginger, cloves, sweet potato
recipes.healthBenefits: Millet is gluten-free and rich in magnesium; fermentation gives mild probiotic benefit; refreshing and energising.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, magnesium, iron, B vitamins
recipes.cautions: Drink fresh - spoils quickly. Limit added sugar.
recipes.servedWith: Masa, akara, on its own
recipes.storageGuidance: Keep chilled in a clean covered container; drink within 1-2 days; discard if it smells off.
recipes.tips: The raw portion contains enzymes that naturally sweeten the drink.

steps.instruction: Soak millet overnight; drain.
Blend with ginger, cloves and sweet potato into a smooth paste; divide into 2 parts.
Pour boiling water into one part while stirring until it thickens.
Add the second (raw) part, stir, cover and leave 2-3 hrs.
Strain through a fine cloth, sweeten and chill.

recipes.name: Ogi / Pap (Akamu)
recipes.originNote: Nationwide (Yoruba: ogi; Igbo: akamu; Hausa: koko)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Fermented maize (or millet/sorghum) paste, water, sugar or honey, milk (optional)
recipes.healthBenefits: Smooth, easily eaten source of carbohydrate energy; pairs well with protein foods (akara, moi moi, eggs, milk) for a more balanced breakfast.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates; B vitamins (amount depends on grain and processing)
recipes.cautions: Plain pap is low in protein and fibre. Pair with beans, eggs or milk and keep added sugar low.
recipes.servedWith: Akara, moi moi, boiled eggs, bread
recipes.storageGuidance: Cooked pap: refrigerate within 2 hrs and eat within 2 days. Settled ogi paste: keep covered with clean water in the fridge, changing the water daily.
recipes.tips: Stir constantly while adding boiling water to avoid lumps. Keep settled ogi covered with clean water in the fridge and change the water daily.

ingredientLines.rawText: 2 cups dry yellow or white maize (or millet/sorghum)
Clean water for soaking, washing and cooking

steps.instruction: Wash the maize and soak in clean water for 2-3 days, changing the water daily, until soft and slightly sour.
Drain and blend with clean water until smooth; sieve through a fine cloth or sieve and discard the chaff.
Leave the sieved liquid to settle for 6-12 hours, then pour off the water; the thick settled paste is ogi.
Mix about 1/2 cup ogi paste with a little cold water into a smooth slurry.
Pour in 2-3 cups boiling water, stirring quickly until it thickens; simmer gently 3-5 min, stirring, so it is fully cooked.
Sweeten to taste and add milk if desired. Serve hot.

recipes.name: Agidi (Eko)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Fermented corn paste (ogi), water, leaf or food-grade wraps
recipes.healthBenefits: Soft, mild carbohydrate food that makes a filling base for protein-rich partners such as moi moi, akara, fish or stew.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates; small amounts of B vitamins
recipes.cautions: Low in protein and fibre on its own, so pair with beans, eggs, fish or meat. Use clean wrappers and refrigerate leftovers.
recipes.servedWith: Moi moi, akara, stew, fried fish
recipes.storageGuidance: Refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 1-2 days.
recipes.tips: The mixture must be thick enough to hold its shape; it firms up as it cools. Use clean wrappers, refrigerate and eat within 1-2 days.

ingredientLines.rawText: 3 cups settled ogi paste (see Ogi / Pap)
About 7 cups water (4 cups boiling, rest cold)
Banana or other clean leaves, or food-grade wraps/moulds

steps.instruction: Mix 1 cup of the ogi paste with 1 cup cold water into a smooth slurry.
Pour in about 4 cups boiling water, stirring quickly until it thickens into a custard-like pap.
Stir in the rest of the paste gradually, then cook on low heat for 10-15 min, stirring, until very thick and glossy.
Scoop portions into leaf wraps or moulds and wrap/cover tightly.
Leave to cool and set (30-45 min). Serve with moi moi, akara or stew.

recipes.name: Fufu (Akpu / Cassava Fufu)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Cassava tubers (soaked/fermented), water
recipes.healthBenefits: Cassava is a staple source of energy; the soft, stretchy dough suits vegetable and protein-rich soups.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates; small amounts of potassium
recipes.cautions: Cassava must be peeled, soaked or fermented and well cooked to reduce naturally occurring cyanogenic compounds; never eat it raw or poorly processed. Low in protein and fibre, so serve with vegetable soups and fish or meat.
recipes.servedWith: Egusi, ogbono, okra, oha, efo riro
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hrs and eat within 1-2 days.
recipes.tips: Never eat raw or poorly processed cassava: soak fully and cook until tender. Ready-made fufu flour is a convenient alternative; follow the pack instructions.

ingredientLines.rawText: Clean water for soaking and cooking

steps.instruction: Cut the peeled cassava into chunks and wash well.
Soak completely in clean water for about 3 days, until soft and slightly sour-smelling.
Rinse, remove any hard fibrous core, then boil the soaked cassava until very tender (20-30 min).
Drain; pound in a mortar (or blend with a little hot water) until smooth and stretchy, removing any fibre strands.
Mould into balls with wet hands and serve hot with soup.

recipes.name: Semovita (Semo)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Semolina (wheat) flour, water
recipes.healthBenefits: Quick-cooking swallow that provides carbohydrate energy and, depending on the brand, some B vitamins and a little protein.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates; some protein; B vitamins (varies by brand)
recipes.cautions: Contains wheat (gluten): not suitable for wheat allergy or coeliac disease. Low in fibre, so pair with vegetable soups.
recipes.servedWith: Egusi, okra, efo riro, ogbono, vegetable soups
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hrs and eat within 1-2 days.
recipes.tips: Add the flour gradually and keep turning to avoid lumps. If too stiff, add a splash of hot water and turn again.

ingredientLines.rawText: About 2 1/4 cups water (plus a little extra if needed)

steps.instruction: Bring 1 3/4 cups of the water to a boil.
Mix about 1/3 cup semovita with the remaining cold water into a smooth paste and stir it into the boiling water to make a thin starch.
Reduce heat and add the remaining semovita gradually, turning firmly with a wooden spoon until no lumps remain.
Cover and steam on low heat for 3-5 min, then turn again until smooth and stretchy.
Mould into a bowl or cling film and serve hot.

recipes.name: Tuwo Masara & Miyan Taushe
recipes.summaryIngredients: Maize flour; pumpkin, groundnut paste, spinach, tomatoes, onions, dried meat or fish, daddawa
recipes.healthBenefits: Pumpkin supplies carotenoids (a source of vitamin A), groundnut paste adds plant protein and unsaturated fats, and spinach adds iron and folate; the maize swallow provides energy.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, protein, carotenoids (vitamin A), folate, iron
recipes.cautions: Groundnuts are a common allergen. Go easy on oil, salt and stock cubes.
recipes.servedWith: Tuwo masara (maize swallow)
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Add the spinach at the end to keep its colour. Add the groundnut paste gradually so it thickens without catching.

ingredientLines.rawText: 2 cups fine maize flour (for the tuwo)
300g beef, goat meat or dried fish

steps.instruction: Boil the seasoned meat with onion and salt for 30 min until tender; keep the stock.
Add the blended tomatoes and pepper to a pot with the pumpkin cubes and cook until the pumpkin is soft; mash it.
Heat the oil, fry the mashed mixture 10 min, then add the meat stock, groundnut paste (dissolved in a little water), daddawa and stock cubes; simmer 15 min.
Add the meat and simmer 5 min; stir in the spinach for the last 3 min.
Tuwo: mix 1/2 cup flour with cold water into a paste, stir into 3 cups boiling water, then add the remaining flour gradually while turning until firm; cover 5 min, turn again and mould.

recipes.name: Ofe Oha (Oha Soup)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Oha leaves, cocoyam paste, palm oil, assorted meat, stockfish, crayfish, ogiri, pepper
recipes.healthBenefits: Leafy oha adds fibre and plant compounds, while stockfish and meat add protein; cocoyam thickens the soup naturally.
recipes.keyNutrients: Protein, fibre, minerals; vitamins from leafy greens
recipes.cautions: Palm oil, assorted meat and stock cubes make it rich: moderate the oil and salt and keep meat portions sensible. Contains fish and crayfish.
recipes.servedWith: Pounded yam, akpu (fufu), eba, semo
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Add the oha leaves last so they stay green with a little bite. The soup keeps thickening as the cocoyam dissolves, so add it gradually.

ingredientLines.rawText: 2 cups fresh oha leaves (shredded by hand)
5 small cocoyam (boiled, peeled and pounded to a paste)
1 kg assorted meat (beef, shaki, cow skin)

steps.instruction: Boil the meats and stockfish with onion, stock cubes and salt until tender; keep about 4 cups of stock.
Add palm oil, ground pepper, crayfish and ogiri to the stock and boil 5-10 min.
Drop small lumps of pounded cocoyam into the soup and simmer 10-15 min until dissolved and thickened.
Stir in the oha leaves and cook only 3-5 min.
Adjust salt and serve hot.

recipes.name: Ofe Nsala (White Soup)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Catfish or goat meat, yam paste (thickener), crayfish, pepper soup spices, utazi leaves
recipes.healthBenefits: Made without palm oil, so it is lighter than many soups; fish provides protein, vitamin B12 and minerals.
recipes.keyNutrients: Protein, vitamin B12, minerals
recipes.cautions: Contains fish and crayfish (shellfish). Cook fish fresh and just until done; watch stock cubes and salt, and reduce pepper for children.
recipes.servedWith: Pounded yam, fufu, eba
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Thicken gradually because the soup keeps thickening as it simmers. Cook the fish briefly so it does not break up.

ingredientLines.rawText: 1 large fresh catfish (or 1 kg goat meat)
200g boiled yam, pounded to a smooth paste
1 tbsp nsala/pepper soup spice mix (ehuru, uda, uziza)

steps.instruction: Clean the catfish, cut into steaks and season with salt, onion and a stock cube.
Boil the fish in the water with onion for 10-15 min; lift out carefully and keep the stock.
Add crayfish, ground pepper and the spice mix to the stock and boil 10 min.
Drop in small lumps of pounded yam and simmer about 15 min until dissolved and the soup thickens.
Return the fish, add the utazi and simmer 3 min. Adjust seasoning.

recipes.name: Catfish Pepper Soup
recipes.summaryIngredients: Fresh catfish, pepper soup spice, scent leaves, onion, scotch bonnet
recipes.healthBenefits: A lean, protein-rich soup that is low in carbohydrate and full of flavour from herbs and spices; the warm broth also adds fluids.
recipes.keyNutrients: Protein, vitamin B12, minerals
recipes.cautions: Very spicy: reduce pepper for children. Cook fish fresh and thoroughly, and watch salt and stock cubes. Contains fish (and crayfish if added).
recipes.servedWith: Boiled yam, plantain, white rice, or on its own
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Do not overcook catfish or it falls apart. Add the scent leaves at the end to keep their aroma.

ingredientLines.rawText: Handful of scent leaves (efirin) or uziza

steps.instruction: Rinse the fish with hot water and season with salt, onion and a stock cube.
Bring the water to a boil with the onion, ground pepper, pepper soup spice and remaining stock cube; boil 5 min.
Add the catfish carefully and simmer 10-15 min until just cooked; avoid stirring hard.
Add the scent leaves and cook 2 min.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot.

recipes.name: Ikokore (Water Yam Porridge)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Water yam, palm oil, smoked fish, crayfish, pepper, onions, ugu or spinach
recipes.healthBenefits: Water yam provides carbohydrate energy; smoked fish adds protein and palm oil contributes carotenoids and vitamin E.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, protein, carotenoids (palm oil), vitamin E
recipes.cautions: Rich in palm oil and salt: use less oil and add leafy vegetables. Contains fish and crayfish.
recipes.servedWith: Eaten on its own; fried fish
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Let the grated yam steam on top before stirring so the lumps hold their shape.

ingredientLines.rawText: 600g water yam (isu ewura), peeled and finely grated
4 tatashe (red bell peppers), 3 scotch bonnet peppers, 1 onion (blended)

steps.instruction: Peel the water yam and grate it finely.
Boil the blended pepper mix for 10 min to reduce.
Add palm oil, crayfish and stock cubes and fry 5-7 min.
Add the smoked fish and water.
Spoon the grated yam in small lumps over the sauce without stirring; cover and simmer on low heat for 20-25 min.
Stir gently, fold in the vegetables for the last 3 min and adjust salt.

recipes.name: Ewa Agoyin
recipes.summaryIngredients: Soft mashed brown beans, dark spicy dried-pepper sauce (palm oil, onions, crayfish)
recipes.healthBenefits: Beans provide plant protein, fibre, folate and iron; slow cooking makes them soft and filling.
recipes.keyNutrients: Plant protein, fibre, folate, iron
recipes.cautions: The sauce is oil-heavy: use less oil and pepper. Beans can cause gas, so soak or pre-boil and discard that water. Contains crayfish.
recipes.servedWith: Agege bread, fried plantain (dodo)
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Fry the sauce slowly on low heat: the dark colour and smoky taste come from patience, not high heat. Keep the beans mashed but not watery.

steps.instruction: Sort and wash the beans; boil in plenty of water on medium heat for about 1 1/2 hrs until very soft, topping up water as needed.
Mash with a wooden spoon until thick and soft; season with salt and cook off excess water.
Sauce: heat the oil and fry the sliced onions until deep brown.
Add the ground dried pepper and crayfish; fry on low heat 10-15 min until very dark and the oil separates; season.
Serve the beans topped with the sauce, with bread or fried plantain.

recipes.name: Ukwa (African Breadfruit Porridge)
recipes.summaryIngredients: African breadfruit seeds (ukwa), palm oil, edible potash, crayfish, dry fish, onions, utazi or ugu
recipes.healthBenefits: Breadfruit seeds provide plant protein, fibre and energy; fish and vegetables add protein and vitamins.
recipes.keyNutrients: Plant protein, fibre, carbohydrates, minerals
recipes.cautions: Usually cooked with edible potash, which adds sodium: use sparingly, and people on a low-sodium diet should check with a doctor or dietitian. Contains fish and crayfish.
recipes.servedWith: Eaten on its own; fried fish, plantain
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: If the seeds are slow to soften, soak overnight or use a pressure cooker to save time and fuel. Add water gradually.

ingredientLines.rawText: 1 tsp edible potash (akanwu), dissolved and filtered
1 cup shredded utazi or ugu leaves

steps.instruction: Pick over and wash the ukwa; boil with the dissolved potash and enough water for 1-1 1/2 hrs until soft, topping up water as needed.
Add palm oil, crayfish, pepper, onion, fish, stock cubes and salt; simmer 15-20 min until the pottage thickens.
Stir in the vegetables and cook 3 min.
Adjust salt and serve hot.

recipes.name: Yam & Egg Sauce
recipes.summaryIngredients: White yam, eggs, tomatoes, onions, scotch bonnet, vegetable oil
recipes.healthBenefits: Yam provides steady carbohydrate energy and potassium; eggs add high-quality protein and vitamin B12; tomatoes and peppers add vitamin C.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, protein, vitamin B12, potassium, vitamin C
recipes.cautions: Use moderate oil and boil rather than fry the yam. Add spinach or bell peppers for extra fibre. Contains egg.
recipes.servedWith: Tea, pap, sliced avocado
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Take the eggs off the heat while still slightly moist so they do not turn rubbery. Salt the yam water lightly for the best texture.

ingredientLines.rawText: 1/2 medium tuber white yam (about 600g), peeled and sliced
3 ripe tomatoes, 1 onion, 1-2 scotch bonnet peppers (chopped)
1 stock cube, 1 tsp curry (optional), salt to taste
1 cup chopped spinach or green pepper (optional)

steps.instruction: Wash the yam slices and boil in lightly salted water for 15-20 min until fork-tender; drain.
Heat the oil, fry the onion 2 min, add tomatoes and pepper and cook 8-10 min until reduced.
Season with stock cube, salt and curry.
Beat the eggs lightly, pour into the sauce and stir gently until just set (2-3 min); add vegetables.
Serve hot with the boiled yam.

recipes.name: Plantain Porridge (Unripe Plantain Pottage)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Unripe plantain, palm oil, crayfish, smoked fish, onion, pepper, ugu or spinach
recipes.healthBenefits: Unripe plantain provides fibre, resistant starch and potassium; vegetables and fish add vitamins and protein.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, fibre, potassium, protein, carotenoids (palm oil)
recipes.cautions: Rich in palm oil: use moderate amounts. Contains fish and crayfish.
recipes.servedWith: Eaten on its own; fried fish, salad
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Mashing a few plantain cubes thickens the porridge naturally without extra oil.

steps.instruction: Heat the palm oil on low heat, lightly fry sliced onion, then add the blended pepper mix and fry 10 min.
Add crayfish, stock cubes, salt and water; bring to a boil.
Add the plantain cubes and smoked fish; cover and simmer 15-20 min until soft.
Mash a few pieces against the pot to thicken; stir in the vegetables and cook 3 min.
Serve hot.

recipes.name: Coconut Rice
recipes.summaryIngredients: Parboiled rice, coconut milk, tatashe, scotch bonnet, onions, stock, mixed vegetables, shrimp or chicken (optional)
recipes.healthBenefits: Coconut milk adds flavour and energy; peppers and vegetables add vitamins and fibre; rice supplies carbohydrates.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, vitamin C, fats (coconut), some minerals
recipes.cautions: Coconut milk is high in saturated fat: use light coconut milk, keep portions moderate and add plenty of vegetables. Contains coconut (and shellfish if shrimp is added).
recipes.servedWith: Fried fish or chicken, salad, plantain
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool quickly, refrigerate within 1 hr; eat within 1 day; reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Add the coconut milk gently and avoid boiling hard, as it can split.

ingredientLines.rawText: 2 tatashe (red bell peppers), 2 scotch bonnet peppers, 1 onion (blended)
2 stock cubes, 1 tsp curry, 1 tsp thyme, salt to taste

steps.instruction: Wash the rice and drain.
Heat the oil, fry a sliced onion, add the blended peppers and fry 10 min.
Add the coconut milk, stock and seasoning and bring to a gentle boil.
Add the rice, stir once, cover tightly and cook on low heat 25-30 min.
Add the vegetables (and shrimp, if using) for the last 5 min, then fluff gently.

recipes.name: Obe Ata (Nigerian Tomato Stew)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Tomatoes, tatashe, scotch bonnet, onions, vegetable oil, beef or chicken, seasoning
recipes.healthBenefits: Tomatoes and peppers supply vitamin C and lycopene; adding protein (meat, fish, eggs, beans) turns it into a more balanced topping.
recipes.keyNutrients: Vitamin C, lycopene, vitamin A (from peppers), protein (if meat added)
recipes.cautions: Stew is often cooked with a lot of oil: use about half, and add vegetables or beans. Watch stock cubes and salt.
recipes.servedWith: White rice, boiled yam, plantain, beans
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Boiling the blend down first removes sourness and water, so you need less oil and less frying time.

ingredientLines.rawText: 2 stock cubes, 1 tsp curry, 1 tsp thyme, 2 bay leaves, salt to taste

steps.instruction: Boil the meat with onion, seasoning and salt until tender; keep the stock.
Blend the tomatoes, tatashe, scotch bonnet and half an onion; boil down in a dry pot for about 20 min and pour off excess water.
Heat the oil, fry sliced onion, add the tomato paste and fry 5 min.
Add the reduced pepper mix and fry 15-20 min, stirring, until the oil floats.
Add the meat, stock and seasoning; simmer 10 min and adjust salt.

recipes.name: Gizdodo
recipes.summaryIngredients: Chicken gizzards, ripe plantain, bell peppers, scotch bonnet, onion, tomato paste
recipes.healthBenefits: Gizzard is a protein-rich meat that also supplies iron and zinc; plantain adds carbohydrates and potassium; peppers add vitamin C.
recipes.keyNutrients: Protein, iron, zinc, potassium, vitamin C
recipes.cautions: Fried plantain and oil add calories: use little oil, or bake or air-fry the plantain. Watch salt.
recipes.servedWith: Drinks, as a party snack, or with rice
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh; cool fully, store covered and eat within 2-3 days.
recipes.tips: Keep the plantain cubes slightly firm so they do not break when tossed in the sauce.

ingredientLines.rawText: 2 tatashe (red bell peppers) and 1 green bell pepper
Oil for frying plus 3 tbsp for the sauce
2 stock cubes, 1 tsp thyme, 1 tsp curry, salt to taste

steps.instruction: Clean the gizzards and boil with onion and seasoning for 30-40 min until tender.
Fry the plantain cubes until golden; drain.
Blend the red peppers with the scotch bonnet and boil down.
Heat the sauce oil, fry sliced onion and tomato paste, add the pepper puree and fry 10 min.
Add the gizzards and a splash of stock; stir in the plantain and green pepper strips and toss 2-3 min.

recipes.name: Okpa
recipes.summaryIngredients: Bambara nut (okpa) flour, palm oil, pepper, salt, water
recipes.healthBenefits: Bambara nut is a legume that provides plant protein, fibre and minerals such as iron; steaming keeps the preparation simple.
recipes.keyNutrients: Plant protein, fibre, iron, carbohydrates
recipes.cautions: Palm oil adds fat: use moderate amounts. Dense and filling, so small portions go a long way.
recipes.servedWith: Eaten on its own, with pap or pepper sauce
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh; cool fully, store covered and eat within 2-3 days.
recipes.tips: Add warm water gradually and stir well for a lump-free batter. Steam above the water rather than boiling directly in it, so the okpa stays firm.

ingredientLines.rawText: Ground pepper and salt to taste
Banana leaves or small containers for steaming

steps.instruction: Whisk the palm oil with the pepper, salt and a splash of water until well blended.
Add the okpa flour gradually with the warm water, stirring until you have a smooth, thick, pourable batter.
Rest the batter for 10 min.
Pour into leaf wraps or small containers and steam, covered, for 40-60 min until set.
Cool slightly, unwrap and serve warm.

recipes.name: Kuli-kuli
recipes.summaryIngredients: Roasted groundnuts, salt, pepper or ginger (optional), oil for frying (optional)
recipes.healthBenefits: A crunchy source of plant protein, unsaturated fats, vitamin E and magnesium; the dry snack keeps well when stored properly.
recipes.keyNutrients: Protein, healthy (unsaturated) fats, vitamin E, magnesium
recipes.cautions: Groundnuts are a common and potentially severe allergen. Energy-dense, so keep portions small. Discard mouldy, shrivelled or bitter nuts and store dry (moulds on groundnuts can produce aflatoxins).
recipes.servedWith: Garri (soaked), pap, akara, or as a snack
recipes.storageGuidance: Store completely dry in an airtight container; discard if rancid, mouldy or bitter (aflatoxin risk).
recipes.tips: Roast on medium heat and stir constantly so the nuts do not scorch. Store completely dry.

ingredientLines.rawText: 3 cups raw groundnuts (shelled; discard any mouldy or discoloured nuts)

steps.instruction: Sort the groundnuts carefully and roast in a dry pan until golden; cool and rub off the skins.
Grind to a thick paste.
Knead with a little warm water and the salt until the oil separates; press and pour off the oil (keep it for cooking).
Shape the remaining dough into thin rolls or small rings.
Fry in hot oil on medium heat 5-8 min until crisp, or bake at 160°C for 25-30 min, turning once.
Cool completely and store in an airtight container.

recipes.name: Roasted Corn & Ube (Agbado ati Ube)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Fresh corn on the cob, ube (African pear), salt
recipes.healthBenefits: A whole-food snack: corn provides fibre and carbohydrates, and ube provides unsaturated fats and fibre.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, fibre, unsaturated fats (ube)
recipes.cautions: Ube is fat-dense, so a little goes a long way. Roast corn until cooked through.
recipes.servedWith: Eaten on its own
recipes.storageGuidance: Best eaten fresh and warm.
recipes.tips: Test the ube with a fingertip: it should be tender, not mushy. Over-soaking makes it oily and soft.

ingredientLines.rawText: 6 fresh corn cobs (peeled or in husk)
Hot (not boiling) water for softening the ube

steps.instruction: Roast the corn over charcoal, or under a hot grill or in the oven, turning often for 15-20 min until the kernels are tender and lightly charred.
Soak the ube in hot (not boiling) water for 5-10 min until tender.
Drain the ube and serve warm with the roasted corn, with a little salt if desired.

recipes.name: Kilishi
recipes.summaryIngredients: Thin beef slices, yaji (groundnut-based spice), groundnut paste, oil, salt
recipes.healthBenefits: A concentrated, protein-rich dried meat snack that is a source of iron, zinc and vitamin B12.
recipes.keyNutrients: Protein, iron, zinc, vitamin B12
recipes.cautions: Dried meats are high in salt and spice: eat small portions. Dry hygienically and store airtight; discard if mouldy or off-smelling. Contains groundnut (peanut).
recipes.servedWith: Eaten as a snack, with drinks
recipes.storageGuidance: Store airtight in a cool, dry place (refrigerate for longer storage); discard if mouldy or off-smelling.
recipes.tips: Even, thin slices dry evenly. Keep flies away while drying, and use a low oven or dehydrator if you cannot sun-dry safely.

ingredientLines.rawText: 1 kg lean beef (topside), sliced very thin
1 cup yaji (ground kuli-kuli, ginger, garlic, paprika, cayenne, stock cube)

steps.instruction: Trim off fat and slice the beef about 3 mm thick.
Dry the slices under a clean net in the sun, or in a low oven (about 70°C, door slightly open), for 4-6 hours until dry but not crisp.
Mix the yaji, groundnut paste, oil, salt and a little water into a thick paste and coat each strip on both sides.
Dry again until firm.
Grill briefly over low heat on both sides until fragrant.
Cool and store in an airtight container.

recipes.name: Dambun Shinkafa
recipes.summaryIngredients: Coarsely ground rice, moringa (zogale) or cabbage, carrot, onion, groundnut oil, pepper, seasoning
recipes.healthBenefits: A steamed (not fried) rice dish; moringa or cabbage add fibre and vitamins, and it pairs easily with eggs or fish for protein.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, fibre, vitamins from vegetables, minerals
recipes.cautions: Add a protein (egg, fish, beans) to balance the meal and use moderate oil. Groundnut oil is a peanut-derived product.
recipes.servedWith: Boiled eggs, fried fish, yaji
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Pulse the rice only briefly: you want coarse grains, not flour. Steam in a basket above (not touching) the water.

ingredientLines.rawText: 2 cups shredded zogale (moringa) leaves or cabbage
Boiled eggs or fried fish to serve

steps.instruction: Pulse the washed rice briefly in a blender to coarse, couscous-like grains; drain.
Steam the rice granules for 20-25 min until just soft.
Fluff and mix in the onion, pepper, carrot, vegetables, oil, stock cubes and salt.
Steam again for 15-20 min until the vegetables are tender.
Serve with eggs or fish.

recipes.name: Danwake
recipes.summaryIngredients: Bean flour, wheat or cassava flour, edible potash, water; served with groundnut oil, yaji, eggs, vegetables
recipes.healthBenefits: Bean-flour dumplings provide plant protein, fibre and slow-digesting carbohydrates; vegetable and egg toppings add vitamins and protein.
recipes.keyNutrients: Plant protein, carbohydrates, fibre, folate
recipes.cautions: Edible potash adds sodium: use sparingly. Toppings such as oil and yaji can be heavy, and yaji contains groundnut. Contains wheat if wheat flour is used.
recipes.servedWith: Boiled eggs, onions, tomatoes, cabbage, yaji, groundnut oil
recipes.storageGuidance: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hrs; eat within 3 days (or freeze); reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.tips: Use the potash sparingly. Knead until smooth so the dumplings hold together.

ingredientLines.rawText: 1/2 tsp edible potash (kaun/kanwa), dissolved in a little water
Toppings: 1/4 cup groundnut oil, yaji, 2 boiled eggs, sliced onions, tomatoes, cabbage

steps.instruction: Mix the bean flour, binder flour and salt.
Add the dissolved potash and warm water gradually, kneading about 5 min into a soft dough that does not stick.
Pinch off small pieces and roll or press into small dumplings.
Boil about 5 cups water, add the dumplings and cook 15-20 min until they float and are cooked through.
Drain and serve with sliced onion, tomato, boiled eggs, a drizzle of groundnut oil and yaji.

recipes.name: Fura da Nono
recipes.summaryIngredients: Millet flour balls (fura), fermented cow's milk (nono), spices, water, sugar (optional)
recipes.healthBenefits: Millet provides carbohydrate energy and minerals; nono adds protein and calcium, making it a filling drink-meal.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, protein, calcium, B vitamins
recipes.cautions: Contains milk (lactose). Use pasteurised or properly boiled-then-fermented milk and clean water: raw milk carries food-safety risks, especially for children, pregnant women and older adults.
recipes.servedWith: On its own, chilled
recipes.storageGuidance: Keep chilled in a clean covered container; drink within 1-2 days; discard if it smells off.
recipes.tips: Chill the nono for the best taste. Use pasteurised or properly prepared milk from a trusted source.

ingredientLines.rawText: 1 tbsp ground ginger, 1/2 tsp ground cloves
About 1/2 cup warm water to bind
4 cups nono (fermented milk) or plain yoghurt

steps.instruction: Mix the millet flour with the ground spices and knead with a little warm water into a stiff dough.
Shape into small balls.
Steam or boil the balls for 30-40 min until cooked through.
Pound or mash the cooked balls until smooth and sticky, then reshape into balls and cool.
To serve, crumble the fura into a bowl, add chilled nono and a little cold water, sweeten if desired and stir.

recipes.name: Kunun Aya (Tiger Nut Drink)
recipes.summaryIngredients: Tiger nuts, dates, coconut, ginger, water
recipes.healthBenefits: Tiger nuts supply fibre and unsaturated fats; dates sweeten the drink naturally, so little or no sugar is needed.
recipes.keyNutrients: Fibre, unsaturated fats, carbohydrates, minerals
recipes.cautions: Calorie-dense for a drink, so keep servings modest. Best chilled and drunk fresh as it spoils quickly; wash tiger nuts well. Contains coconut if added.
recipes.servedWith: Drunk chilled, on its own
recipes.storageGuidance: Keep chilled in a clean covered container; drink within 1-2 days; discard if it smells off.
recipes.tips: Wash the tiger nuts thoroughly and chill promptly. Add a little extra date for sweetness instead of sugar.

ingredientLines.rawText: 2 cups tiger nuts, sorted and washed

steps.instruction: Sort and wash the tiger nuts, then soak in clean water for 2-3 hours (or overnight) to soften.
Drain and blend with the dates, coconut and ginger in 3-4 cups of the water until fine.
Strain through a clean muslin or fine sieve, squeezing out all the milk.
Add the remaining cold water, stir and chill.
Serve cold; refrigerate and drink within 2-3 days.

recipes.name: Garri Soakings
recipes.summaryIngredients: Garri, cold water, roasted groundnuts, sugar or honey, milk or coconut (optional)
recipes.healthBenefits: A quick, affordable energy food; groundnuts add protein and healthy fats, and milk or coconut add extra nutrients.
recipes.keyNutrients: Carbohydrates, protein and fats (from groundnuts/milk)
recipes.cautions: Garri alone is mostly starch and low in protein, fibre and vitamins: add groundnuts, milk, fish or fruit. Limit added sugar and use clean water. Contains groundnut/milk if added.
recipes.servedWith: Roasted groundnuts, coconut, fried fish, kuli-kuli
recipes.storageGuidance: Prepare and eat immediately.
recipes.tips: Add the water slowly because garri swells. Pair with groundnuts or milk to make it more balanced.

steps.instruction: Put the garri in a bowl and add the cold water gradually, stirring.
Add sugar or honey and milk, if using; let it swell for 1-2 min.
Top with groundnuts or coconut and serve immediately.
